newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Nov factory orders off but some backlogs rise.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Nov factory orders off but some backlogs rise.

text.p: New orders received by U.S. factories moved lower in November, the Commerce Department said Tuesday, partially reversing a strong showing in October.
The department said orders fell 0.4 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of $320.5 billion, after being up a revised 1.1 percent in October.
However, shipments of finished products and order backlog continued to rise suggesting some underlying vitality in the economy's industrial sector as the year neared its end.
Orders for costly durable goods like new cars and large home appliances that are intended to last three years or more fell 1.5 percent to $172.3 billion after being up 0.6 percent in October.
Previously the department said October factory orders had risen 0.9 percent.
Wall Street analysts, for their part, had forecast a decline of 0.6 percent for November.

The weaker showing was likely to be good news on Wall Street where investors had worried of late that the economy may be strong enough to begin generating inflation, prompting Federal Reserve interest rate hikes.
The department had previously reported that orders of durable goods in November fell 1.6 percent, reducing that slightly in the current report.
Orders for nondurables like food and paper products, however, continued to show healthy increases, rising 0.8 percent after being up 1.6 percent in October.
Among durable products, electronic and electrical equipment had the largest drop, falling 9.1 percent, after being up 17.2 percent in October.
The department said shipments rose 0.9 percent while unfilled orders were up 0.4 percent. Inventories rose 0.4 percent, also.
